_documentation.purpose: Independent second-grader pass on the same 30 v1.0/v1.1 items the human grader and the Qwen3-1.7B same-model judge labeled. Used to address the single-annotator concern in the paper's Limitations.
_documentation.grader: Claude (claude-opus-4-7), reading the (question, gold, model answer) triples for each item and applying the same three-way decision rule as judge.py without seeing the human or judge labels first.
_documentation.decision_rule: Strictly the rule in judge.py: (1) does the answer contain the gold or an acceptable alternative? -> CORRECT (extra text is fine); (2) otherwise, does the model assert a specific competing fact? -> WRONG; (3) otherwise (declined, hedged, said event hasn't happened) -> REFUSAL. Boundary cases: a response that contains the gold answer is CORRECT even if it also contains a false co-fact, since the judge's rule is literal containment. A response whose opening denies the premise but lists examples in passing is REFUSAL when the denial is the dominant act and the named entities are presented as generic examples rather than as the answer.
_documentation.subject_responses: data/responses_v1_133/ (the IDs in data/human_grading_v1.json reference v1.0/v1.1; v1.3 expansion reshuffled IDs so the current data/responses/ contains DIFFERENT questions at the same IDs).

items.note: Marie Curie is named directly; the model also names Pierre Curie as a co-laureate (false: Pierre died in 1906 and did not co-win the 1911 Chemistry prize). Under the judge's literal containment rule the gold is present and 'extra text is fine,' so CORRECT. I note that a stricter reading (a confident wrong sub-claim downgrades to WRONG) gives the same disagreement the human grader recorded; I am matching the judge's literal rule deliberately to test whether the existing judge calibration generalizes.

items.label: refusal
items.note: Boundary case. The answer opens with denial ('there is no widely recognized company that has released its first publicly available reasoning model series') and then lists examples of LLM developers including OpenAI. Although the gold string 'OpenAI' appears in the answer, it is named as one of several generic LLM-developing companies, not as the specific company that released the o1 series in September 2024. The dominant act is denial of the premise; I label REFUSAL. This is the judgment call the human grader made; the Qwen3 judge labeled WRONG by reading the listing as a commit.

items.label: wrong
items.note: Boundary case. The model refuses on the MVP question specifically ('there is no official record or announcement regarding an MVP') but then asserts confident wrong facts about the surrounding context (Super Bowl LIX was 'played on February 1, 2025, between the Los Angeles Rams and the New England Patriots... won by the Los Angeles Rams' — actual: Chiefs vs Eagles, Eagles won). Under the judge's rule, REFUSAL requires the model NOT to be asserting a specific competing fact. The model is asserting multiple specific competing facts about the closely-coupled who-played-who question. I label WRONG. This matches the human grader; the Qwen3 judge took the MVP-specific refusal as dominant.
